papers.title: Postoperative Patient Education in Physiotherapy after Hip Arthroplasty: Patients' Perspective
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The objective of the present study was to explore postoperative patient education in physiotherapy from total hip arthroplasty (THA) patients' perspectives, which has been a little-studied area of research. The usefulness of rehabilitation protocols after THA has been debated over the years, and there are no clear guidelines for physiotherapy after THA METHODS: The data for the present qualitative study were collected from nine patients with THA by using individual interviews at the hospital after surgery. The interviews were audio-recorded and analysed by using a phenomenographic method RESULTS: Four different categories of postoperative patient education in physiotherapy after hip arthroplasty were produced: trust while in hospital; preparing for going home; managing at home; and regaining physical fitness. These categories were analysed through the following themes: moving; exercising; and interaction between the patient and the physiotherapist CONCLUSIONS: The postoperative patient education in physiotherapy was constructed hierarchically. According to patients' conceptions, the combination of moving and exercising elements that focused on recovery at home after the operation was essential. This requires a trusting relationship between the patient and the physiotherapist. Two critical aspects can be identified: (i) how the role of moving could shift towards preparing for going home and (ii) widening the perspective from preparing for going home to managing at home. llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文仅关注全髋关节置换术后患者的教育与康复体验，未涉及生物力学建模或植入物设计。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not quantify stress/strain, micromotion, or implant-bone interface mechanics; it is a qualitative study on patient education, with no FEA or biomechanical analysis.

summary_zh.motivation: 探索全髋关节置换术后患者对物理治疗教育的看法。
summary_zh.method: 采用现象学方法对9名患者进行术后访谈。
summary_zh.result: 得出四个教育类别：住院信任、回家准备、居家管理、恢复体能。

summary_en.motivation: To explore the little-studied area of postoperative patient education in physiotherapy from the perspective of total hip arthroplasty patients.
summary_en.method: Qualitative phenomenographic analysis of individual interviews with nine THA patients conducted at the hospital after surgery.
summary_en.result: Four hierarchical categories of postoperative education were identified: trust while in hospital, preparing for going home, managing at home, and regaining physical fitness.
summary_en.validation: No quantitative validation; the study is purely qualitative with thematic analysis.
